body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 16, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm one — expect a high near 98° today under mostly clear skies. Overnight, our crews handled a serious wrong-way crash on Highway 99 that left three dead, along with a palm tree fire that reached an apartment complex in southeast Bakersfield. Air quality is moderate at 97 AQI. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just before 1 a.m., when a wrong-way driver traveling northbound in the southbound lanes of Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road collided with two other vehicles. Firefighters and medics worked to extricate two patients from the wreckage, while a third vehicle caught fire. The original call drew a heavy rescue response, with Metro 3, medic squad 63, and Truck 65 on scene. Earlier in the evening, around 9:16 p.m., a palm tree fire spread to the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way off Villalobos Street. Engine 7 took incident command as additional units rolled in to battle the flames. Around the county, officers staged on a possible shooting call on Price Street that never materialized on the air, chased a DUI driver in a white BMW fleeing east from the 33rd Street area, and handled a string of domestics and disturbances — including one at a Camellia Village apartment where a wall was damaged.

## Today's weather

We’re in for another warm August day, with temperatures climbing to a high of 98° under mostly clear skies. The overnight low is expected to dip to around 72°. As of this morning, it’s already 91° at Meadows Field. No weather alerts are active for Kern County at this time, and air quality is moderate at an AQI of 97. Stay cool and hydrated if you’ll be out and about today.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that three people are dead following a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early this morning.** According to the California Highway Patrol, a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes near 7th Standard Road when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado around 12:44 a.m. The Honda caught fire in the crash, and all three occupants inside were killed. The driver and another occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries, while the two occupants of the Chevrolet suffered minor injuries. It is unknown at this time if alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

**KGET 17 tells us a man was arrested in Bakersfield following a domestic violence standoff involving minors.** Bakersfield Police Department officials said the incident began when a man barricaded himself inside a residence with children present. After a period of negotiation, the man was taken into custody without incident. The children were safely removed from the situation, and no injuries were reported. The arrest highlights the ongoing challenges local law enforcement faces in addressing domestic violence cases that involve vulnerable family members.

**Bakersfield Now reports that the 90s are back as a third heatwave settles over Bakersfield, though a Pacific trough is expected to bring “cooler” highs.** After a brief respite, temperatures are once again climbing into the 90s, marking the third heatwave of the summer season for Kern County. Meteorologists note that while the current spell may not break records, it will still bring elevated heat risks to the area. Residents are advised to stay hydrated and limit outdoor activities during the hottest parts of the day.

## Something good

In a boost for local infrastructure, both the Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports are set to receive a portion of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This investment will support improvements and upgrades at our regional airports, ensuring safer and more efficient travel for residents and visitors alike. It’s a welcome development for our community’s connectivity and economic growth.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar for Kern County residents. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. Later in the week, the Planning Commission gathers on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. 

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full lineup of shows starting next week. On August 22, catch Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio. Comedian Rodney Carrington takes the stage on August 27, followed by Cumbiatron: The Cumbia Rave on August 28. August 29 features two shows: Willie Barcena in the afternoon and a Michael Jackson tribute by Michael Phoenix in the evening. Rounding out the month, the Mi Historia Tour featuring Leyendas del Mariachi USA comes to the Fox on September 4. Be sure to check venue details and ticket availability if you plan to attend.
